analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. Two files changed: docs/provider/cli-reference.md and docs/reference/configuration.md. No executable code, keys, attestation paths, wire formats or authorization logic are touched.

cli-reference.md: the changed lines are the benchmark flag table entries (`--runtime-concurrency`, `--runtime-stagger`, around lines 519 and 1145-1146). These describe local diagnostic modes. They state that prefix caches stay off and that nothing is downloaded. The reviewed head text also keeps the existing statements on LaunchAgent environment passthrough, App Attest worker opt-in, logout/enroll behavior and report upload bounds. None are weakened. The flags add no new network surface, secret exposure or coordinator interaction.

configuration.md: two environment switches are added, `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED` and `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY` (lines 316-317). Both are default-on MTP scheduling and decode-history toggles. They are documented as not forwarded to LaunchAgents, consistent with the other inference tunables. They touch TB-007 (inference engine) performance behavior only. They do not change prefix-cache storage, TTL, HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt scoping or KEK handling, so the T-041 posture is unchanged. The implementation lives in the libs/mlx-swift-lm MTPContractsV2.swift file. That file is not in this batch, so the claimed behavior (carry/hidden-state handling, no cross-request leakage) is unverified here. If the corresponding source change is reviewed elsewhere, it should check that carried hidden states are per-request and are cleared on slot reuse (T-028).

No finding. The residual uncertainty is the unseen implementation of the new MTP behavior, which this docs PR only describes.
